nodes.name: Hot-press target fabrication
nodes.procedure: Commercial nickel, iron, and molybdenum powders were homogenously mixed for 12 h using a dry ball milling process. The as-mixed powders were then carefully poured into a graphite mold with a copper plate as the back support. After that, the mold was transferred into the chamber of the hot-press machine. After approximately 30 min of pumping, the chamber was refilled with argon while the pump was turned off. The hot-press procedure was performed at 400°C for 30 min under 300 psi of hydraulic pressure. After allowing the target to cool down naturally, it was carefully taken from the mold and polished with sand paper.

nodes.name: Magnetron sputtering deposition
nodes.procedure: Prior to the sputtering process, the sputtering chamber was firstly evacuated to a low vacuum with a rotary pump, and then to a high vacuum with a turbomolecular pump for 1 h until the pressure reached 10^{-6} torr. After that, the pre-sputtering was conducted at a low power of 30 watts for about 20 min to remove the surface contamination. Keeping a working distance of 10 cm from the substrate, the target was then sputtered at 300°C with a power of 70 watts for 30 min. The entire sputtering procedure was carried out with argon as the working gas at a pressure of 9.5×10^{-3} torr.

nodes.characterization_summary: As-sputtered MoNiFe alloys MNF-0 and MNF-2 exhibit no visible diffraction peaks, confirming amorphous nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the representative X-ray diffractions of MNF-0 and MNF-2 have no visible peaks, similar to the spectrum from Si substrate. This result suggests that the as-sputtered MoNiFe alloy has an amorphous nature

nodes.characterization_summary: As-sputtered MNF-n (n=0,1,2,3) films show flat, smooth, compact surfaces with fine granular particles uniformly coated on nickel foam substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: All the as-sputtered MoNiFe-alloy clearly shows a flat, smooth, and compact surface with fine granular particles that are uniformly coated throughout the nickel foam substrate, as depicted in Fig. 1a-d.

nodes.characterization_summary: MNF-2 cross-section shows catalyst film thickness of ~140 nm; HRTEM confirms amorphous nature with no regular atomic arrangement; SAED shows blurry pattern.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the thickness of the catalyst can be precisely calculated to be about 140 nm. Fig. 3b shows the high-resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) image. It can be clearly seen that there is no regular arrangement of atoms... The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of MNF-2 in Fig. 2c displays a blurry image

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping of MNF-2 shows Ni, Fe, Mo homogeneously distributed throughout the sample with lower Mo signal intensity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3b-d shows that Ni, Fe, and Mo are homogenously spread out through the sample, with less signal intensity of the Mo element due to its much lower concentration.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER MNF-2 shows Raman peak at 482 cm⁻¹ related to Ni-O vibration in NiOOH phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman analysis in Fig. 9b clearly exhibits a peak at around 482 cm⁻¹. According to the previous study, the Raman peak at about 480 cm⁻¹ is related to the Ni-O vibration in the NiOOH phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER MNF-2 XPS shows Ni³⁺ peaks at 855.9 and 873.3 eV confirming in-situ NiOOH formation; Mo and Fe peaks shifted slightly.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The binding energies at 855.9 and 873.3 eV are attributed to the spin orbitals of Ni³⁺ 2p3/2 and Ni³⁺ 2p1/2, respectively, which did not exist for the fresh MNF-2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER MNF-2 anode shows nanosheet structure formation indicating surface phase transformation; post-HER cathode morphology unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the morphology of MNF-2 catalyst after being used as the anode to perform the OER was totally different... Fig. 9a clearly exhibits the formation of the nanosheet structure... MNF-2, after being used as the cathode for executing the HER, did not exhibit any significant morphological differences
